style: Gives crew time to explain and guides them when clarification is needed
Detailed inspection with emphasis on crew knowledge, records and emergency arrangements
Questions ratings and engineers directly on their own duties
Checks alarms on the alarm signal column one by one

questions.q: Show me the equipment. What is the purpose of this system?
What are the hot work precautions?
Where are the emergency escapes and what do you do in an emergency?
Where are the ESD and remote stops, and when would you use them?
How do you operate the emergency steering?
What are your actions in a blackout?
What are the hours of rest rules, and what do you do if you have a non-conformity?
How do you report a near miss?
What does this alarm mean, what caused it, what do you do and who do you inform?

checks.item: Seawater pumps and pipelines maintenance records
Alarm signal column, each alarm checked
Oily water separator and its alarm
FO temperature records, FO and LO analysis reports
Bunker SDS and the fuel in use with its storage temperature
Manning level against company manning policy

tips: Ratings must be able to show the equipment, explain its purpose and say what they would do and who they inform
Engineers should explain procedures from real onboard practice, then point to the SMS procedure
Know every alarm on the alarm column: what it means, the cause, the action and who to call
summary: An engine room heavy inspection. Ratings and engineers were questioned directly on emergencies, alarms, hot work and escape routes, and the alarm column was checked alarm by alarm. Port and date were not given in the report.
